correctness.rationale: A complete vertex-link parity covering argument proves b >= ceil(o/4) on simple closed triangulations. Two different standalone integer algorithms exhaust all 3^12 icosahedral spin assignments, agree on all 13 occupation-sector minima and counts, and check the lower convex hull with slopes -2,-1,1,3,4,5. The C++ checker independently verifies critical degeneracies and the 20 minimal three-edge defect supports, each of size six. The exact-domain quantifiers are J>0, all real h, and named icosahedral graph edges; no floating-point numerics or incomplete search support the proof.

value.rationale: The finite regular icosahedron is a canonical maximally triangular Platonic spin cluster, in which q=3 antiferromagnetism is topologically frustrated. The sharp general parity bound gives a structural reason for the exact three-bond deficit; the full 13-sector exact census yields six distinct critical fields, seven favored-color occupation plateaux, twenty frustration-support types and substantial critical degeneracy. These are naturally defined physical observables and are not implied numerically by chromatic-number facts or a generic transfer-matrix representation. No general bulk phase behavior is claimed.
